title: Saving Private Ryan
synopsis: Omaha Beach, June 6, 1944. The ramp goes down. By the next week you're crossing France for one man whose brothers all died. Earn this.

nodes.text: Spray, vomit, prayer. The ramp goes down.

choices.consequence: “Lead off” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Brave.
There is no taking “Go side” back. Smart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Water, blood, sand. The seawall ahead.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Survive.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Brave—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Captain Miller's hand shakes. Orders are quiet.

choices.consequence: “Steady the men” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Lead.
“Wait” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: Bangalore. The wall breaches. The pillbox falls.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Take prisoners.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
“Take none” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Cold.

nodes.text: Find Ryan. One of four brothers. Three are dead.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Argue the order.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Take it.” The story records the instinct as “Soldier” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Reiben, Mellish, Caparzo, Wade, Jackson, Upham, Horvath.

choices.consequence: “Brief them” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Lead.
You commit to “Let Miller.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Sniper. A child handed across rubble.

choices.consequence: “Save the child” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Mission.

nodes.text: Sniper takes Caparzo. Jackson takes the sniper.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Mourn briefly” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Anger.

nodes.text: A pinned squadron. A choice to engage or skirt.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Engage.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Mission.

nodes.text: You take it. Wade is killed in the assault.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Mercy.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Anger.

nodes.text: Wade is dead. The German shovels. Reiben wants him shot.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Shoot him.” The story records the instinct as “Anger” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Reiben refuses to march. The squad almost shatters.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Hold them together.” The story records the instinct as “Lead” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Let Reiben go.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Miller's hand shakes. He cries. The squad doesn't see.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.

nodes.text: Ryan, alive, won't leave his men. The bridge must be held.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Help hold it.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
“Carry him out” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Mission.

nodes.text: Cover, sticky bombs, ambush, fallback to alamo.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.
You commit to “Improvise.” The story records the instinct as “Speed” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: They arrive. The bombs work imperfectly.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hold” back. Brave shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Smart.

nodes.text: House by house. Mellish dies in a knife fight upstairs.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Brother.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Mission.

nodes.text: Upham freezes on the stairs. He does nothing.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Forgive him later.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Hate him later” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Captain Miller is hit at the bridge. He shoots a tank with a pistol. The P-51s arrive.

choices.consequence: “Hold his hand” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Mission.

nodes.text: Earn this, he says. He dies.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Years later you stand at the cross. Your family behind you.

choices.text: Ask your wife if you've been a good man
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Quiet—follows you into whatever comes next.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You live a life worth earning. You marry kindly, work hard, raise children who do good. You never say much about the war. They know anyway.
You teach high school history for decades. You don't bring up Normandy. The kids find it in books. They come to your desk after class. You answer carefully.
You don't talk about it. Your wife knows. Your children, eventually, know. Your grandchildren learn the soft version. The truth is, somehow, both.
